solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lots of pasta doesn't require a starter

indicators.note: going without a starter means the word's opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a common type of pasta

explanation.surface: A huge plate of pasta is filling enough that nobody needs a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a first course, but it is the first letter of NOODLES, which goes, leaving OODLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, so it matches plenty or heaps of something.

clue.text: Fight to get horse placed in disputed result

indicators.note: a disputed result is one called into question and argued over, so its letters are thrown into disorder
putting something inside another means these letters go within the others

parts.note: the six letters of this word rearranged
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out over a contested horse race placing.
explanation.walkthrough: Gee-gee is the nursery word for a horse; 'placed' hints at racing but here it signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To struggle is to grapple or battle with someone, the same as engaging in combat.

clue.text: Musical performance at home with a squeeze?

parts.note: a public performance of music
someone at home is in
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical evening held at home, perhaps with a romantic partner, or squeezebox.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: the instrument is played by squeezing its bellows, and it is nicknamed a squeezebox.
explanation.definitionFit: A concertina is a small hexagonal bellows instrument, played by pressing it in and out, hence a playful definition.

clue.text: Opportunity to understand deer on tourist attraction

parts.note: a hind is a female deer
places tourists go to see are the sights

explanation.surface: Seeing deer at a tourist spot gives a chance to learn about them.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindsight is looking back after the event, which gives the chance to grasp what really happened.

clue.text: The odds on batting against this bowling

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds in horse or greyhound racing
the side batting in cricket is in

explanation.surface: A bookmaker quotes the odds on a batsman facing a particular kind of bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is said to be 'in', and SP is the bookies' starting price.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is cricket bowling where the ball is made to turn sharply off the pitch, as opposed to pace.

clue.text: What might precede work party?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word that goes before 'work' in the name of a caring profession
second meaning: an informal gathering of friends

explanation.walkthrough: Social work is the profession of local welfare care; a social is also a casual get-together.
explanation.definitionFit: The word forms the phrase for welfare casework and is also a noun for an informal gathering or knees-up.

clue.text: Investigation might scare her into action

indicators.note: put into action, the letters are set moving and come out in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A police inquiry might frighten a woman into doing something.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is systematic study or enquiry, the same as a careful investigation into a subject.

clue.text: Open letters from military settlement

parts.note: flowers that are out are open
letters delivered are the post

explanation.surface: Someone opens mail sent home from an army base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open letters' reads as a verb and its object, but each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a small remote station of troops, a garrison set apart from the main force.

clue.text: Army on exercises get record

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Soldiers on manoeuvres set a new record.
explanation.definitionFit: To tape something is to make a recording of it, so as a verb it means capture on a recording medium.

clue.text: Single test covering end of term is better

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so this piece goes inside the others

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to test something is to prove it

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the closing letter of this word

explanation.surface: A student's lone end-of-term exam shows progress.
explanation.walkthrough: I and PROVE together wrap the M, which sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To better something, used as a verb, is to make it superior or raise its standard.

clue.text: Platform for a meal outside a flat

indicators.note: something outside another surrounds it, so one word's letters enclose the other

parts.note: a midday meal
taken as written
pad is slang for a flat or home

explanation.surface: Someone sets out a meal on a terrace outside an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' of 'a meal' is not part of the meal: it is the letter tucked inside LUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch pad is the structure rockets lift off from, a raised base for blast-off.

clue.text: Make enquiries about individual racket

indicators.note: going about something means going around it, enclosing it

parts.note: to nose about is to pry or make enquiries
I as one, an individual

explanation.surface: Someone digs into a lone operator's shady scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' looks like a scam to be investigated, but it means din.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud unpleasant din, and noise is the general word for such sound.

clue.text: Sweetener for tabloid America backed

indicators.note: backed means put into reverse, so the joined letters are read from the end

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a cheap newspaper
the United States

explanation.surface: A sweet inducement for an American tabloid that's supported financially.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is the classic ingredient added to food and drink to make it sweet.

clue.text: Almost cause offence — a right to be keeping to oneself

indicators.note: almost the whole word means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to insult is to cause offence
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone claims a right to privacy even if it offends.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular people are inward-looking and detached, like an island cut off from others.

clue.text: Pros rest up after playing champions

indicators.note: once played about with, the letters come out in a different order

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Professional sportsmen put their feet up after a match against title holders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champions' looks like winners, but here it means backers, as a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Champions of a cause are those who back and defend it, which is what fans and advocates do.

clue.text: In sum, a great egg well cooked

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new form

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Summing up a meal: it was a superb, well-cooked egg.
explanation.definitionFit: In aggregate means taken as a whole total, so the phrase 'in sum' matches it.

clue.text: Getting arrested for having a lack of finance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally, being caught, since to pinch is slang for to arrest
second meaning: the idiom for suffering from being short of money

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a 'pinch' is an arrest, so the money idiom can also be read as being nicked by police.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes hardship from tight money, and read literally names the experience of being nabbed by police.

clue.text: Love comes between truth and the belly for such a worker

indicators.note: coming between two things means sitting inside the pair, flanked on both sides

parts.note: a fact is a truth
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
tum is informal for the stomach

explanation.surface: Romance gets caught between honesty and appetite for some labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is an employee who does all kinds of jobs, a general-purpose servant or worker.

clue.text: Educated miners on energy charge

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British coal miners' union
E is the physics symbol for energy
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Well-schooled miners are charged for their power.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerate means competent with numbers and arithmetic, schooled in mathematics as literate is in reading.

clue.text: Horseman, hearing of dispatched gold, started to run

indicators.note: hearing of a word means taking how it is heard, not how it is written

parts.note: dispatched means sent; it is spelt differently but sounds the same
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: started means we use only where the next word begins

parts.note: the opening letter of 'run'

explanation.surface: A rider hears news that gold has been sent and starts running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horseman' suggests a rider, but the creature is literally half man, half horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A centaur is the mythical creature with a man's upper body and a horse's body, literally a horse-man.

clue.text: Topless pundits worried by one who shows all

indicators.note: with no top, the word loses its opening letter
worried letters are agitated and disturbed, ending up in a fresh order

parts.note: the experts' word without its head

explanation.surface: Commentators are disturbed by a topless exhibitionist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' and 'shows all' paint a naked scene, but 'Topless' only beheads the word for experts.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist goes without clothes, so naturally displays everything, hence a witty descriptive phrase.

clue.text: Energy required for a high power low return

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the pieces are read from the end

parts.note: HP is the standard abbreviation, as in horsepower
to low is to make the sound a cow makes

explanation.surface: Electrical energy needed for a power plant giving poor returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' sounds like the opposite of high, but it is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for vigour or vitality, the get-up-and-go of someone full of energy.

clue.text: Ship found in healthy bit of bother?

indicators.note: being found in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A vessel in good condition still has some trouble aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassle is informal for annoyance or inconvenience, a minor bother or trouble.

clue.text: Criminal record provided by bench

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for a history of convictions
second meaning: a long seat without a back, as in a school

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests magistrates on the bench; instead a bench is a long seat, as in a school classroom form.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang someone with previous convictions 'has form', and a long backless seat is also called one.

clue.text: Gathered round to protect return of the rule of law

indicators.note: a return heads back, so the letters are read from right to left
to protect something is to hold it inside, so the letters lie within the words

parts.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: People gather round to defend the restoration of law and order.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits backwards across 'gatheRED ROund'.
explanation.definitionFit: Order is the state of peace where laws are obeyed and society is controlled.

clue.text: About to get morning paper

parts.note: re means about or concerning
am is ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: Someone is about to fetch the morning newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morning paper' reads as a newspaper, but the paper is a quantity of sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a standard bundle of 500 sheets, so it is a measure of writing paper.

clue.text: Favours that offer grounds to be worried

indicators.note: worried letters are agitated and stirred up, so they come out in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Kind deeds can give someone reasons for concern.
explanation.definitionFit: Good turns are kindly acts done for others, which is what favours are.

clue.text: A social climber must begin by riding

parts.note: a jockey riding is said to be up
to begin is to start

explanation.surface: An ambitious newcomer has to make their start on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Begin by riding' puts the riding piece in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen in status who behaves arrogantly, a pushy social climber.

clue.text: Ruin — and one short story of the marriage

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
I is the Roman numeral one
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A wrecked marriage, and a brief tale of the wedded couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital is the adjective for matters concerning wedlock and married couples.
